title: Huawei says Ascend tops Nvidia in China as demand gap remains
key_facts: According to ijiwei, Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu spoke at the Huawei Connect (HC) conference in Shanghai about Ascend AI chips.
Xu said Ascend has likely surpassed Nvidia in China, based on data Huawei can track; Nvidia's exact market share is difficult to determine.
Xu said Huawei is selling everything it can produce and domestic demand still far exceeds supply.
The Ascend 950PR, designed mainly for inference, is available in limited volumes; the 950DT-based SuperPoD for training is in testing, with volume expected around end-2026 or early 2027.
Huawei has supplied small volumes of Ascend 950 SuperPoDs to a few countries, has no plans for a broad international rollout, and is prioritising Chinese customers.
Xu expects the global AI computing chip supply-demand balance to largely recover around 2029, with China potentially taking longer.
quote_evidence: Meanwhile, Xu said Ascend has likely surpassed NVIDIA in China based on data Huawei can track, though NVIDIA’s exact market share is difficult to determine.
Xu said Huawei is selling everything it can produce and hopes its supply chain will expand faster.
why_it_matters_hint: A company claim that Huawei's chips lead Nvidia in China; supply, not demand, is the constraint Huawei describes.
event_date: early Oct 2026 (Huawei Connect, Shanghai; exact day not stated)
notes: Chunk source digitimes returned only a teaser (181 characters), so the claims were read on TrendForce, which reports them citing ijiwei; the ijiwei original was not opened. Score lowered from 6 to 5: a company claim on market share that cannot be independently checked.
